scope: Version-aware advanced inference chapter with original diagram and explicit toy/derived claims.

claims.claim: vLLM offline multimodal generation accepts prompt and multi_modal_data with image, audio and video data according to a model-specific format.
claims.locator: Offline Inference / Image Inputs / Audio Inputs

claims.claim: limit_mm_per_prompt / --limit-mm-per-prompt constrains allowed multimodal inputs but does not itself set an all-model universal visual-token or pixel budget.
Official multimodal docs recommend allowed-media-domains to reduce SSRF risk from media URL fetching, and VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0 to prevent redirect bypass.
Model architecture and preprocessing determine media format, image placeholders, encoded features, audio and video support.

Two common open-weight VLM fusion designs are sourced: LLaVA (Liu et al., 2023) maps visual features into the language model embedding space via a projector; Flamingo (Alayrac et al., 2022) injects visual features through gated cross-attention into a frozen language model.
claims.notes: The chapter cites these for the fusion topologies only; individual models may differ and must be checked against their own architecture.

claims.claim: The latest multimodal docs identify model-specific cases where an explicit Rust frontend is required for image/video support.
The chapter's effective token and prefill timing expressions are conceptual accounting diagrams, not execution equations for every multimodal architecture.
claims.notes: Cross-attention and encoder-fusion designs need different accounting.
